A website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru: patients book visits, emergency info, plus doctor profiles, a health blog, and Kannada/Hindi versions

@CEO, the brief leaves three choices open that change risk and external commitment, so I need your call before I write the charter. My default is A on each; tell me if you disagree.
1. Q1 Booking: the site is one static file with no backend. A) Booking is a request form that opens WhatsApp/phone callback, and the hospital confirms the slot by phone. No patient data is stored, so privacy risk is low, but no live slots. B) Form posts to a third-party form service. Staff get requests by email, but patient health details pass through a vendor (DPDP Act exposure, needs Requester sign-off on the vendor). Default: A.
2. Q2 Facts and content: doctor profiles, emergency numbers and blog posts need real data. A) Use clearly labelled placeholders, never invented credentials or phone numbers, and block 'done' until the Requester supplies the real emergency number, address and doctor list. Slower, but no false medical or contact info can go live. B) Fill with plausible sample content and flag it. Faster demo, but a fake emergency number or doctor could be mistaken for real. Default: A.
3. Q3 Kannada/Hindi: A) Machine-translate all pages and mark them 'pending native review'. Full coverage, but errors possible. B) Translate only emergency and booking pages fully, keep other pages English with a language switch note. Smaller accuracy risk, partial coverage. Default: A, with emergency text kept short and numeric so it is hard to mistranslate.

@Identity, I chose A on all three, because the brief is silent on vendors and sample data and A carries the least external risk.
1. Q1: A. The booking form is a request that opens WhatsApp/phone callback and the hospital confirms the slot by phone. No patient data is stored and no vendor is involved. Trade-off: no live slots. Chosen because the brief is silent on a vendor, and a vendor would need Requester sign-off under the DPDP Act.
2. Q2: A. Use clearly labelled placeholders and never invent credentials or phone numbers. Block 'done' until the Requester supplies the real emergency number, address and doctor list. Trade-off: slower. A fake emergency number is a patient-safety risk, so this is not negotiable. Pause the run with these questions to @Requester once the layout is built.
3. Q3: A. Machine-translate all pages into Kannada and Hindi and mark each 'pending native review'. Keep emergency text short and numeric, and show the English version beside it on the emergency page. Trade-off: translation errors are possible until a native speaker reviews. Chosen for full coverage, which the brief asks for.
